paragraphs.text: “Isaiah.” Heb., Yesha·ʽeyaʹhu, meaning “Salvation of Jehovah”; LXXBagster(Gr.), He·sa·iʹas; Lat., I·sa·iʹas.
Meaning “My Strength Is Jehovah.” Heb., ʽUz·zi·yaʹhu.
Meaning “Jehovah Is Perfect”; or, “May Jehovah Complete.” Heb., Yoh·thamʹ.
Meaning “He [Jehovah] Has Taken Hold.” Heb., ʼA·chazʹ.
“Its owner.” Heb., beʽa·lavʹ, a pl. form of baʹʽal, to denote excellence.
Or, “left over to us survivors, we should easily have become.”
“Uncanny power, state of taboo,” KB, p. 20; LXX, “fasting.”
“Your,” fem. sing., addressed to Zion, the once “faithful town,” in vs 21.
“The [true] Lord.” Heb., ha·ʼA·dhohnʹ; Gr., ho De·spoʹtes. See App 1H.
Lit., “O house of Jacob,” sing., but the verb “come” is pl.
Or, “they shake hands,” that is, have close association.
Or, “and you do not pardon them.”
Or, “all desirable articles of show; all works of art.”
“The earthling man.” Heb., ha·ʼa·dhamʹ. Compare vs 11 ftn.
“From before the fear of the Lord [Gr., Ky·riʹou], and from the glory of his strength,” LXX. See vs 10 ftn. Compare 2Th 1:9.
“Breath.” Heb., nesha·mahʹ, the same word as in Ge 2:7.
Lit., “and man of war.” Heb., weʼishʹ mil·cha·mahʹ.
Lit., “one lifted up as to face.”
Or, “one skilled at serpent-charming.” See App 7A.
Or, “Just a look at their faces”; or, “Just their showing regard for faces.”
“Children are their task assigners,” by a correction of M.
Or, “on their feet they shake bangles.”
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
“Your,” fem. sing., referring to Zion, or Jerusalem.
Lit., “may your name be called upon us.”
Or, “the sprouting (sprout) of Jehovah.” T, “the Messiah (Christ) of Jehovah.”
Lit., “what has escaped of Israel,” that is, the escaped ones.
Lit., “what remains,” that is, the remnant.
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
Lit., “a horn the son of oil.”
Lit., “O inhabitant,” sing. but in a collective sense.
“And . . . men of.” Heb., weʼishʹ, sing. but in a collective sense.
“Those dead from hunger,” TSy and two Heb. mss.
“Sheol,” M(Heb., sheʼohlʹ)T; Gr., haiʹdes; Syr., shiul; Lat., in·ferʹnus. See App 4B.
“Its soul.” Heb., naph·shahʹ; Gr., psy·khenʹ; Lat., aʹni·mam. See App 4A.
“Her,” fem. sing., referring to Jerusalem. See vs 3.
“And the [true] God.” Heb., weha·ʼElʹ. See App 1G.
“Saying: ‘Quickly let Jehovah hasten his works,’ ” Sy.
“The righteous one,” LXXVg and a few Heb. mss; 1QIsaMSy, “the righteous ones.”
“To a great nation.” Heb., lag·goh·yimʹ, pl. to denote greatness, but with a sing. pronoun (“it”) and with a sing. verb, thus, “it will . . . come in.” See vs 27 ftn.
Lit., “it,” that is, the “nation,” sing. but in a collective sense.
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
Or, “the palace.” Heb., ha·heh·khalʹ, as in 2Ki 20:18; Lat., temʹplum. See Mt 23:16 ftn.
“And the house began to be filled with smoke,” James Washington Watts (1979). See App 3C.
“Which,” pl., M; SyVg and about 100 Heb. mss, “which,” fem. sing.
Or, “be out of the stump of it,” if there was a homoeoteleuton in M.
“Has settled down; has rested,” by another derivation of the Heb. verb.
Or, “a blast.” Heb., ruʹach. See Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force.”
Meaning “A Mere Remnant (Those Remaining Over) Will Return.”
“As Sheol” (Heb., sheʼoʹlah), by a slight change in vowel pointing as suggested in BHK and BHS ftns and in agreement with AqSymThVg; M(Heb.), sheʼaʹlah, “do ask.” See App 4B.
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
“The maiden (young woman).” Heb., ha·ʽal·mahʹ; LXX(Gr., par·theʹnos)Sy(Syr., bethul·thaʼ), “the virgin”; AqSymTh(Gr.), ne·aʹnis, “maiden; girl”; Lat., virʹgo, “virgin.” See Ge 24:16 ftns.
“Immanuel.” Heb., ʽIm·maʹnu ʼEl, meaning “With Us Is God”; Gr., Em·ma·nou·elʹ; Vgc(Lat.), Em·maʹnu·el. See Mt 1:23.
“For the flies.” Heb., laz·zevuvʹ, sing. but in a collective sense.
“And for the bees.” Heb., welad·devoh·rahʹ, sing. but in a collective sense.
That is, the hair of the genitals, according to BDB, p. 920.
Meaning “Hasten, O [or, Hastening to the] Spoil! He Has Come Quickly to the Plunder.”
Meaning “Sender,” designating a water conduit; LXX, “Siloam.”
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
“Know,” LXX and by a correction of M, in agreement with the parallel expression “give ear.”
“God is with us.” Heb., ʽim·maʹnu ʼEl; LXX, “Jehovah God is with us.”
“May admonish me away,” by another derivation of the Heb. verb.
Lit., “it,” fem., that is, the land or earth.
“With no brightness,” by a slight correction; LXX, “so as not to see”; M, “[into which] one is pushed (thrust).”
Lit., “it,” fem., that is, the land or earth.
Or, “the circuit.” Heb., Gelilʹ; Syr., Geli·lo; Gr., Ga·li·laiʹa; Lat., Ga·li·leʹae. “Galilee” later designated the Roman province north of Samaria.
MLXX end chapter 8 here with this as vs 23.
“For it,” MmarginTSy and about 20 Heb. mss.
Or, “the princedom; the rule as prince.” Heb., ham·mis·rahʹ; Gr., he ar·kheʹ; Lat., prin·ci·paʹtus.
Lit., “Wonder (Miracle) of a Counselor,” or, “Wonder, Counselor,” M; LXX, “The Angel of Grand Counsel”; Sy, “Wonder and Counselor.”
Or, “Mighty Divine One.” Heb., ʼEl Gib·bohrʹ (not ʼEl Shad·daiʹ as in Ge 17:1, where see ftn); Sy, “Mighty God of times indefinite”; Lat., Deʹus forʹtis.
Or, “Peaceable Prince,” that is, a prince giving peace.
“The princely rule.” Heb., ham·mis·rahʹ. Here and in vs 6 are the only occurrences of this expression.
Or, “His princely rule will certainly abound, and there will be no end to peace,” if a dittography in M; LXX agrees.
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
Lit., “one lifted up as to face.”
“Has been set afire,” by a correction of M in agreement with TLXX; by another correction, “has been led astray,” similar to Vg.
Lit., “to spoil a spoil and to plunder a plunder.”
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
Or, “the Grand One,” pl. in Heb., possibly to denote the grandeur of an individual.
“The [true] Lord.” Heb., ha·ʼA·dhohnʹ; Lat., Do·mi·naʹtor. See App 1H.
“That is faltering,” according to a different root of the verb.
Or, “Those remaining over,” as in vs 20.
“A mere remnant will return.” Heb., sheʼarʹ ya·shuvʹ, the same Heb. expression as the name “Shear-jashub” in 7:3, where see ftn.
“The Mighty God.” Heb., ʼEl Gib·bohrʹ. See 9:6 ftn, “God.”
Or, “those remaining over,” as in vs 20.
Possibly oil as used for the torches of Gideon’s 300 men; or oil with which the kings of Israel were anointed.
“And . . . a sprout.” Heb., weneʹtser. See Mt 2:23 ftns.
“Will be fruitful,” 1QIsaM; LXXSyVg, “will shoot up”; T reads, “And there will go forth a king from the sons of Jesse, and from the sons of his sons the Messiah (Christ) himself will be brought up.”
“Spirit of.” Heb., ruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma; Lat., spiʹri·tus. See Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force.”
“The earth.” Heb., ʼeʹrets; according to a correction suggested in Gins., ʽa·ritsʹ, “the tyrant.” Compare 13:11 ftn, “Tyrants.”
“As a signal.” Heb., lenesʹ; Lat., in siʹgnum.
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
“Cut off,” KB, p. 334; by another derivation of the Heb. verb, “devote to destruction; banish.” Compare Le 21:18, “with his nose slit.”
“Glow,” BDB, p. 744; by a correction according to KB, p. 728, “full might.”
“Jah.” Heb., Yah. See Ex 15:2 ftn, “Jah”; Ps 68:4 ftn.
“Jah Jehovah.” Heb., Yah Yehwahʹ. This combination occurs only here and in 26:4.
Or, “population,” fem. sing., considered collectively as a woman.
“To my sanctified ones,” that is, sanctified for Jehovah’s war. Heb., lim·qud·da·shaiʹ; Lat., sanc·ti·fi·caʹtis meʹis. Compare Joe 3:9 (4:9 in M).
Lit., “The sound of.” See Ge 4:10 ftn, “Listen.”
“From the Almighty.” Heb., mish·Shad·daiʹ. Compare 9:6 ftn, “God.”
Lit., “and their Kesils.” See Job 9:9 ftn, “Kesil constellation.”
“Productive land.” Heb., te·velʹ; Gr., oi·kou·meʹnei, “inhabited earth”; Lat., orʹbis, “circle,” that is, of the earth. See Mt 24:14 ftn, “Earth.”
“Than the gold of.” Heb., mik·keʹthem. See Job 28:16 ftn.
“The haunters of waterless regions.” Or, “the demons.” T, “apes”; LXXSyVg, “wild beasts.”
Or, “hairy creatures.” TLXXSy, “demons”; Vg, “shaggy creatures.” Compare Le 17:7 ftn, “Demons”; 2Ch 11:15 ftn.
“Come to a stop.” Or, “ceased.” Heb., sha·vathʹ.
Or, “might; power.” See VT, Vol. VII, 1957, pp. 202, 203. 1QIsa(Heb.), mar·he·vahʹ, “assault”; LXXSy, “the taskmaster”; Vg, “the tribute.”
“Those impotent in death.” Heb., repha·ʼimʹ; LXXSyVg, “the giants.” Compare Job 26:5 ftn; Ps 88:10 ftn.
“Shining one,” BDB, p. 237; Heb., heh·lelʹ. Gr., ho he·o·sphoʹros, “the bringer of dawn (morn)”; Lat., luʹci·fer, “light bearer.” Compare Job 38:32 ftn, “Mazzaroth constellation.”
“God.” Heb., ʼEl; Lat., Deʹi; LXX, “the heaven.”
“The man.” Heb., ha·ʼishʹ; Gr., ho anʹthro·pos; Syr., gab·raʼ; Lat., vir.
Or, “and the remainder of you.” Heb., u·sheʼe·ri·thekhʹ.
According to 1QIsaM; T, “to the houses of Dibon”; Sy, “to the house of Ribon”; Vg, “The House and Dibon.”
“Bring in,” masc. pl. in 1QIsaM, but in MmarginLXXVg and 11 Heb. mss it is fem. sing.
“The oppressor,” by a slight correction; M, “the squeezer.”
Or, “grand owner.” Heb., ba·ʽalehʹ, a pl. form of baʹʽal, possibly to express grandeur.
Or, “because upon your summer fruit and upon your harvest the [battle] shout has fallen.”
“You,” fem., referring to the city of God’s worship.
Or, “a nation long and smooth,” that is, a tall and smooth-faced people.
“Of elasticity,” by reading two Heb. words as one word of two syllables, as in 1QIsa; M, “of measuring line, of measuring line.”
“Spirit mediums.” Agents used as a vessel of a demon of divination. Lat., py·thoʹnes. See Ac 16:16.
“Master.” Heb., ʼadho·nimʹ, pl. of ʼa·dhohnʹ, to denote majesty, modified by the sing. adjective “hard.”
“Her,” evidently referring to the land, fem.; LXX, “them.”

“Tearing Down.” M(Heb.), ha·Heʹres; 1QIsa(Heb.), ha·Cheʹres, “the Sun”; Syr., He·res; Lat., Soʹlis, “(of) the Sun”; Gr., A·se·dekʹ, a transliteration of the Heb. word hats·tseʹdheq, “the righteousness.” (See Gins.Int, pp. 406, 407.) T paraphrases to read: “(City of) the House of the Sun, which is to be destroyed.”
Or, “deal Egypt a blow, dealing [it] a blow and healing [it].” In Heb. the latter two verbs are in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.
In Heb. these four verbs are in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
“Men.” Heb., ʼish, sing. but in a collective sense.
Lit., “O that which is trampled down [in threshing] belonging to me!”
“Dumah” (meaning “Silence”), MTSyVg; LXX, “Idumea,” that is, the land of the Edomites.
“Against the desert plain.” Heb., baʽ·ravʹ (ʽaravʹ corresponds to ʽara·vahʹ, according to KB, p. 733); SyVg, “Arabia.”
“You,” fem., addressed to the “city,” fem., in vs 2.
“Cry,” either a cry for help or a war cry.
“Your,” fem. sing., referring to the “daughter of my people” in vs 4.
Lit., “a land broad on both sides (hands).”
“Your master.” Heb., ʼadho·neyʹkha, pl. of ʼa·dhohnʹ, to denote excellence.
Lit., “to my servant.” Heb., leʽav·diʹ; Lat., serʹvum meʹum.
Meaning “My Portion Is Jehovah.” Heb., Chil·qi·yaʹhu.
“And your dominion.” Heb., u·mem·shel·tekhaʹ; Gr., oi·ko·no·miʹan sou, “your stewardship.”
“As for his master.” Heb., kaʼ·dho·navʹ, pl. of ʼa·dhohnʹ, to denote excellence.
Lit., “has turned as evening; has become dark.”
Lit., “the lights.” Evidently, the eastern region or horizon.
“You will deliver them from wicked men,” LXX. Compare 2Th 3:2.
Or, “spirit.” Heb., ruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma; Lat., spiʹri·tus. See Ge 1:2 ftn, “Force.”
“In Jah Jehovah.” Heb., beYahʹ Yehwahʹ. See 12:2 ftn, “Jehovah.”
“And now fire will consume those in opposition,” LXX. Compare Heb 10:27.
“A corpse of mine.” Heb., neve·la·thiʹ, sing. but likely in a collective sense, “Corpses of mine”; LXX, “Those in the memorial tombs”; Vg, “My killed ones.”
“Foaming wine.” AlCa(Heb.), cheʹmer; that is, fermenting wine.
Lit., “the valley of fatnesses [or, fertile soils].”
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.

Lit., “For it is ’tsaw upon tsaw, tsaw upon tsaw, qaw upon qaw, qaw upon qaw, a little here, a little there,’ ” as an imitation of the sounds of the prophet’s speech. Heb., ki tsaw la·tsawʹ tsaw la·tsawʹ, qaw la·qawʹ qaw la·qawʹ, zeʽehrʹ sham zeʽehrʹ sham.
“Here I am laying,” in agreement with TLXXSyVg; M, “Here I am, [the One that] has laid.”
“In Zion a stone.” Heb., beTsi·yohnʹ ʼaʹven; Gr., Si·onʹ liʹthon; Lat., in Siʹon laʹpi·dem; Syr., beTs·hiun kiʼ·phaʼ; T(Aram.), beTsi·yohnʹ meʹlekh, “in Zion a king.”
Or, “a corner of meeting for foundation with foundation.” The expression “a sure foundation” is lit., “foundation, foundation.”
“Wheat, millet.” Or, “wheat in rows.” The meaning of the second Heb. word is uncertain.
Or, “in the appointed time”; or, “in the determined portion.” The meaning is uncertain.
Possibly meaning “The Altar Hearth of God”; or, “The Lion of God,” referring to Jerusalem.
“You,” fem. sing., referring to the town.
Lit., “smear yourselves over, and be smeared over.” Compare 6:10, “paste their very eyes together.”
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
“They will sanctify.” Heb., yaq·diʹshu; Gr., ha·gi·aʹsou·sin; Lat., sanc·ti·fi·canʹtes.
Or, “form an alliance,” by pouring out a libation. Or, “interweave a covering.”
“To skim water from a marshy place.” See VT, Vol. VII, 1957, pp. 203-207.
“A thousand will tremble,” by a correction; M, “A thousand, one.”
“A God of judgment.” Heb., ʼElo·hehʹ mish·patʹ.
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
“Your Grand Instructor.” Lit., “your instructors.” Heb., Moh·reyʹkha, pl. to denote grandeur or excellence and thus with a sing. verb.
“Your,” sing., referring to each one’s, MVg; TSy, “your,” pl.
“And his spirit (breath).” Heb., weru·chohʹ; Gr., pneuʹma; Lat., spiʹri·tus.
“Rock of.” Heb., Tsur; TSy, “the Powerful One”; LXX, “the God”; Vg, “the Strong One.”
“With processions of the wave offering,” by slight corrections.
“His Topheth,” by a different vowel pointing; M, “Tophteh.”
“Breath of.” Heb., nish·mathʹ, as in Ge 2:7.
Or, “Passing over.” Heb., pa·soʹach, a form of pa·sachʹ, from which Passover (Peʹsach) is derived.
“Will not be pasted together,” by a slight correction of M, in agreement with TSyVg; M, “will not look.”
“You,” T, eight Heb. mss and four printed ed.; 1QIsaM, 20 Heb. mss and seven printed ed., “him.”
“Our,” TSyVgc and some Heb. mss; 1QIsaM and some Heb. mss, “their.”
“Their very heroes.” Heb., ʼer·ʼel·lamʹ; the meaning is uncertain.
Or, “it has been taken by lice.”
Lit., “it,” fem., referring to the land or earth, fem.
“Her,” referring to Bozrah, the capital of Edom.
Heb., li·lithʹ; likely a nocturnal bird.
“The mouth of Jehovah,” five Heb. mss; 1QIsaSy, “his mouth”; LXX and Arabic, “Jehovah”; MVg, “my mouth.” See BHK and BHS ftns; see also App 1A.
Lit., “her.” Or, “it.” That is, a place, such as Bozrah.
“It,” fem., referring to the “desert plain” in vs 1.
“It,” fem., referring to the “desert plain” in vs 1; 12 Heb. mss, “you.”
Lit., “her,” possibly referring to a wild beast.
Or, “and the Holy Way.” Heb., wedheʹrekh (fem.) haq·qoʹdhesh; Lat., viʹa sancʹta.
“It,” masc., referring to the “highway” (Heb., mas·lulʹ, masc.).

“And by no means will the unclean one pass along there; no unclean way will be there. But the dispersed ones will walk on it and will by no means go astray,” LXX; Sy, “And no uncleanness will pass along in it. And there will be no way beside it, and fools themselves will not wander about there”; Vgc, “No polluted one will pass over it, and this will be for you a direct way, so that the foolish ones may not err in it.”
“It,” fem., referring to the “Way” (Heb., deʹrekh, fem.) in vs 8.
Meaning “My Portion Is Jehovah.” Heb., Chil·qi·yaʹhu.
“Egypt.” Heb., Mits·raʹyim (in the dual number), used for Egypt as a whole, including Upper and Lower Egypt. Compare 37:25 ftn.
Or, “Aramaic language.” Heb., ʼAra·mithʹ; Gr., Sy·ri·stiʹ; Lat., Syʹra linʹgua.
“The Jews’ language.” Heb., Yehu·dhithʹ; Gr., I·ou·da·i·stiʹ; Lat., Iu·daʹi·ce.
“Your lord.” Heb., ʼadho·neyʹkha, pl. of ʼa·dhohnʹ, to denote excellence.
Lit., “the place of breaking through.” Compare 66:9.
“His lord.” Heb., ʼadho·navʹ, pl. of ʼa·dhohnʹ, to denote excellence.
“The living God.” Heb., ʼElo·himʹ chai; the adjective chai, “living,” is sing., although ʼElo·himʹ is pl.
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
“Grass of the roofs, which is scorched before the east wind. (28) Your rising up,” 1QIsa.
“His god.” Heb., ʼelo·havʹ, pl. of ʼelohʹah, to denote the excellence of “Nisroch,” the false god.
“Land of Ararat,” MVg; TSy, “land of Kardo”; LXX, “Armenia.”
Lit., “Let there be a going.” In Heb. this is a verb in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal. See Jer 2:2 ftn, “Go.”
“Jah, even Jah.” Heb., Yah Yah; Sy, “Jehovah”; T, “the fear-inspiring One, Jehovah”; Lat., Doʹmi·num Doʹmi·num. See Ex 15:2 ftn, “Jah”; Ps 68:4 ftn.
“Inhabitants of the system of things,” eight Heb. mss.
By a slight correction; M, “of my shepherd.”
“I have cried for help,” by a slight correction of M.
One of 134 scribal changes from YHWH to ʼAdho·naiʹ. See App 1B.
“You yourself have held back my soul,” by changing one letter in M to agree with LXXVg.
“The God of you men.” Heb., ʼElo·heh·khemʹ.
“Her military service.” Heb., tseva·ʼahʹ, sing. of tseva·ʼohthʹ, translated “armies” in 39:5.
Or, “twice the amount.” Heb., kiph·laʹyim, dual. See Job 11:6 ftn, “Manifold.”
Or, “A voice! There is one calling out”; or, “There is the voice of one calling out.”
Or, “calling out: ‘Through (In) the wilderness clear up the way.’ ”
Or, “A voice! There is one saying”; or, “There is the voice of one saying.”
Lit., “a third part,” of a measure not now known.
“Dynamic energy.” Heb., ʼoh·nimʹ, pl.; Lat., for·ti·tuʹdi·nis, “fortitude.”
Lit., “and from my God.” Heb., u·me·ʼElo·haiʹ.
Or, “coastlands,” that is, of the Mediterranean Sea.
“The God of Israel.” Heb., ʼElo·hehʹ Yis·ra·ʼelʹ.
Lit., “that gods you are.” Heb., ki ʼelo·himʹ ʼat·temʹ.
“Something nonexistent,” by a slight correction in agreement with 1QIsaTSy; M, “hurtfulness; something hurtful.”
“He will . . . be crushed.” Heb., ya·rutsʹ, in agreement with ra·tsutsʹ (“crushed”) in vs 3a.
“And in his name nations will hope,” LXX. See Mt 12:21.
“The Grand One stretching,” pl. in Heb., apparently to denote grandeur or excellence.
“Breath.” Heb., nesha·mahʹ, the same noun as in Ge 2:7.
Or, “one in a covenant of peace.”
“You,” sing., Vg and about 60 Heb. mss; TLXXSy, “you,” pl.; M, “he.”
Or, “atonement price for you.” Lit., “your covering.” Heb., khoph·rekhaʹ.
In agreement with TSy; MLXX, “All the nations have collected themselves together.”
“It is the truth!” Lit., “Truth!” Heb., ʼemethʹ.
“You are my witnesses.” Heb., ʼat·temʹ ʽe·dhaiʹ, pl.; Lat., vos teʹstes meʹi.
“Even my servant,” M(Heb., weʽav·diʹ, sing.)LXXVg; T(Aram.), we·ʽav·dhiʹ me·shi·chaʼʹ, “even my servant, the anointed”; Sy, “servants.”
Or, “and after me there came [or, will come] to be none.”
“The bars of the prisons,” by a correction; M, “the bars, all of them”; Vg, “all the bars (barriers).”
Or, “I, Jehovah, am your Holy One.” Heb., ʼaniʹ Yehwahʹ Qedho·shekhemʹ.
Lit., “and the strong one,” sing. but in a collective sense.
Or, “let us enter into controversy; let us plead.”
“Jeshurun” (meaning “Upright One,” an honorary title for Israel), M; Vg, “Most upright one”; LXX, “beloved Israel”; TSy, “Israel.”
“Let him stand up, let him call out,” LXX.

“And as their witnesses.” Heb., weʽe·dheh·hemʹ. The next word (hemʹmah, “they [are]”) is marked with extraordinary points by the Sopherim, indicating that it should be canceled because of being merely a dittography of the pronominal ending (hem, “their”) of the word preceding it. The pronoun for “they” is also absent in Sy. Accordingly the passage should read: “and as their witnesses they [the darlings; the carved images] see nothing and know nothing, in order that they [the formers of the carved image] may be ashamed.” Ignoring the extraordinary points, the passage would read: “and they [Heb., hemʹmah] are their witnesses that see nothing and that know nothing, in order that they may be ashamed.” See App 2A.
Or, “for an earthling man.” Heb., leʼa·dhamʹ.
Lit., “He also makes a god [Heb., ʼel].”
“It,” that is, the fuel; possibly tree branches.
“Lowest parts,” M; LXXSy, “foundations”; Vg, “extreme parts.” Compare Ps 63:9 ftn.
That is, from the mother’s womb.
“Even in [my] saying,” MSy; LXX, “the One saying”; Vg, “I who say.”
“To his anointed one.” Heb., lim·shi·chohʹ; Gr., khri·stoiʹ; Syr., lam·shi·cheh; Lat., chriʹsto.
Or, “he will send away.” Heb., yeshal·leʹach.
“You,” fem., referring to a people or a city.
“God is in union with you.” Lit., “in you [is] God.” Heb., bakh ʼEl.
